# Setup

This notebook puts the four sources side by side without a model.
Each survey in each country is one **cell**, and each source is one line.
Where the lines of two sources disagree in the same country and period, the gap is a difference between the instruments (wording, mode, and which vote they ask about), not a change in the electorate.
Notebook 2.6 models these gaps; this notebook shows what the model starts from.

```{r}
#| label: setup

# To track render duration
start_time <- Sys.time()

# set width of console output
options(width = 80)

# Install and load required packages
p_required <- c(
  "tidyverse",
  "here",
  "arrow",
  "sessioninfo"
)
packages <- rownames(installed.packages())
p_to_install <- p_required[!(p_required %in% packages)]
if (length(p_to_install) > 0) {
  install.packages(p_to_install)
}
sapply(p_required, require, character.only = TRUE)
rm(p_required, p_to_install, packages)

# Shared tree helpers: countries_25, ctype_levels, n_eff()
source(here("code", "00_helper", "pid_tree.R"))
```

# Load the Type Files

Notebooks 2.1--2.4 each write one row per respondent with the common composition type (`tree_ctype()` in `pid_tree.R`):

- **explicit**: attached, voted for the same party;
- **mismatched**: attached to one party, voted for another;
- **denier**: no attachment, reported a party vote (voting leaners included, as a survey without a leaner probe would count them);
- **attached non-voter**: attached, no party vote reported;
- **non-partisan**: no attachment, no party vote (non-voting leaners included).

Attachment DK, studies without a vote item, and attached voters whose two answers cannot be compared have no type and are left out of every denominator.

```{r}
#| label: load

types <- c("eu25", "ees", "cses", "ess") |>
  map(\(s) read_parquet(here("data", "02_processed", paste0(s, "_types.parquet")))) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(source = factor(source, levels = c("ESS", "EES", "CSES", "EU25")))

# Respondents per source, with and without a type
types |>
  count(source, typed = !is.na(ctype)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = typed, values_from = n, names_prefix = "typed_")

# Weights used, by source
types |>
  distinct(source, survey, country, weight_source) |>
  count(source, weight_source)
```

# Cells

One row per survey × country × type.
`share_w` is the weighted share, `share_u` the unweighted one.
`n` is the cell's unweighted number of typed respondents and `n_eff` its Kish effective sample size, $(\sum w)^2 / \sum w^2$, which shrinks `n` by how uneven the weights are.
The interval is a 95% Wilson interval computed with `n_eff` in place of `n`, so it reflects sampling noise under the weights, nothing else.

```{r}
#| label: cells

# Wilson interval for a share p from n observations
wilson <- function(p, n, z = 1.96) {
  centre <- (p + z^2 / (2 * n)) / (1 + z^2 / n)
  half <- z * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2)) / (1 + z^2 / n)
  list(lo = centre - half, hi = centre + half)
}

typed <- types |>
  filter(!is.na(ctype))

# Cell totals
cell_totals <- typed |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_eff = n_eff(weight),
    w_total = sum(weight),
    vote_ref = first(vote_ref),
    # Several where a cell pools samples (EES 2004 GB)
    weight_source = paste(sort(unique(weight_source)), collapse = " + "),
    .by = c(source, survey, country, year)
  )

cells <- typed |>
  summarise(
    k = n(),
    k_w = sum(weight),
    .by = c(source, survey, country, year, ctype)
  ) |>
  # Zero cells for types absent from a survey
  complete(
    nesting(source, survey, country, year),
    ctype,
    fill = list(k = 0L, k_w = 0)
  ) |>
  left_join(cell_totals, by = c("source", "survey", "country", "year")) |>
  mutate(
    share_w = k_w / w_total,
    share_u = k / n,
    lo = wilson(share_w, n_eff)$lo,
    hi = wilson(share_w, n_eff)$hi
  ) |>
  select(source, survey, country, year, vote_ref, weight_source, ctype, k, n, n_eff, share_w, share_u, lo, hi) |>
  arrange(source, country, year, ctype)

# Shares add up to 1 in every cell
cells |>
  summarise(w = sum(share_w), u = sum(share_u), .by = c(survey, country)) |>
  (\(d) stopifnot(all(abs(d$w - 1) < 1e-9), all(abs(d$u - 1) < 1e-9)))()

# Cells per source
cell_totals |>
  summarise(
    cells = n(),
    countries = n_distinct(country),
    years = paste(min(year), max(year), sep = "-"),
    median_n = median(n),
    median_n_eff = round(median(n_eff)),
    .by = source
  )

write_parquet(cells, here("data", "02_processed", "composition_cells.parquet"))
```

The cell table is written to `data/02_processed/composition_cells.parquet`.
It is the input of notebook 2.6 and the table of raw numbers behind every modelled share.

# Coverage and Overlap

Notebook 2.6 can only tell a source difference from a change over time where two sources observe the same country at about the same time.
The first table counts, per country, the cells of each source.
The second lists the **overlaps**: pairs of cells from two different sources in the same country at most one year apart.

```{r}
#| label: coverage

cell_totals |>
  count(country, source) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  arrange(country) |>
  print(n = 25)
```

```{r}
#| label: overlap

overlaps <- cell_totals |>
  select(country, source, survey, year) |>
  (\(d) inner_join(d, d, by = "country", suffix = c("_a", "_b"), relationship = "many-to-many"))() |>
  filter(
    as.integer(source_a) < as.integer(source_b),
    abs(year_a - year_b) <= 1
  )

# Overlaps per source pair
overlaps |>
  count(source_a, source_b, name = "overlaps") |>
  arrange(desc(overlaps))

# Countries with an overlap per source pair
overlaps |>
  summarise(countries = n_distinct(country), .by = c(source_a, source_b))
```

# Trajectories by Type

One figure per type, with the 25 countries as panels on one y-axis.
Each source is a line with its own colour and point shape, each point a survey, each bar its 95% interval.
The EES and EU25 ask about the European Parliament vote, the CSES about the current lower-house vote and the ESS about the last national election, so the types built from the vote (explicit, mismatched, denier, attached non-voter, non-partisan) differ between sources for that reason as well as for the wording.
Each figure has a weighted and an unweighted tab.

```{r}
#| label: plot-helper

# Okabe-Ito, validated (dataviz); shapes as the second encoding
source_colours <- c(ESS = "#0072B2", EES = "#E69F00", CSES = "#009E73", EU25 = "#CC79A7")
source_shapes <- c(ESS = 16, EES = 17, CSES = 15, EU25 = 18)

type_titles <- c(
  "explicit" = "explicit partisans",
  "mismatched" = "mismatched partisans",
  "denier" = "deniers",
  "attached non-voter" = "attached non-voters",
  "non-partisan" = "non-partisans"
)

plot_trajectory <- function(type, weighted = TRUE) {
  d <- cells |>
    filter(ctype == type) |>
    mutate(
      share = if (weighted) share_w else share_u,
      lo = if (weighted) lo else NA_real_,
      hi = if (weighted) hi else NA_real_,
      country = factor(country, levels = countries_25)
    )
  ggplot(d, aes(x = year, y = share, colour = source, shape = source)) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.6, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_point(size = 1.4) +
    facet_wrap(vars(country), ncol = 5, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = source_colours, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = source_shapes, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2000, 2010, 2020), labels = c("'00", "'10", "'20")) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, NA)) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1996, 2024)) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Share of", type_titles[[type]]),
      subtitle = if (weighted) {
        "Weighted shares with 95% intervals (Kish effective n); one point per survey"
      } else {
        "Unweighted shares; one point per survey"
      },
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL,
      colour = NULL,
      shape = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "top",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
}
```

# What the Weights Change

The largest differences between weighted and unweighted shares, in percentage points, over all cells.
The EU25 cells are unweighted and so do not appear.

```{r}
#| label: weight-diff

cells |>
  mutate(diff_pp = round(100 * (share_w - share_u), 1)) |>
  filter(source != "EU25") |>
  arrange(desc(abs(diff_pp))) |>
  select(source, survey, country, ctype, n, share_u, share_w, diff_pp) |>
  mutate(across(c(share_u, share_w), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  print(n = 20)

# Typical shift by source and type
cells |>
  filter(source != "EU25") |>
  summarise(
    median_abs_pp = round(100 * median(abs(share_w - share_u)), 2),
    max_abs_pp = round(100 * max(abs(share_w - share_u)), 1),
    .by = c(source, ctype)
  ) |>
  arrange(source, ctype)
```

# Leaners

Only surveys with a leaner probe (the CSES studies that fielded it, and EES 2009) can split the deniers.
The figure shows, in those cells, the weighted share of deniers who say they lean toward a party when probed.
Wherever there is no probe, these leaners are counted among the deniers.

```{r}
#| label: leaners

# Cells where the probe was fielded
probed <- types |>
  filter(!is.na(lean)) |>
  distinct(source, survey, country)

leaner_cells <- types |>
  semi_join(probed, by = c("source", "survey", "country")) |>
  filter(ctype == "denier") |>
  summarise(
    leaner = sum(weight * (lean %in% "yes")) / sum(weight),
    n = n(),
    .by = c(source, survey, country, year)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    lo = wilson(leaner, n)$lo,
    hi = wilson(leaner, n)$hi
  )

leaner_cells |>
  summarise(cells = n(), median_leaner_share = round(median(leaner), 2), .by = source)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-leaners
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 9

leaner_cells |>
  mutate(country = factor(country, levels = countries_25)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = leaner, colour = source, shape = source)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 1.4) +
  facet_wrap(vars(country), ncol = 5, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = source_colours) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = source_shapes) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2000, 2010, 2020), labels = c("'00", "'10", "'20")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1996, 2024)) +
  labs(
    title = "Leaners among deniers, where a probe was fielded",
    subtitle = "Weighted share of no-attachment voters who lean toward a party; 95% intervals",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    colour = NULL,
    shape = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

# Caveats

- **The sources ask about different votes**: EP vote (EES, EU25), current lower-house vote (CSES), last national election (ESS). Every type except the attachment itself depends on the vote.
- **The wordings differ**: the ESS asks for a party one feels *closer to than all the other parties*, the CSES and EES whether one is *close to* a party, the CSES then probes the rest. See notebooks 2.1--2.4.
- **The intervals are sampling intervals.** They say nothing about wording, mode, coverage or nonresponse beyond what the weights correct.
- **EU25 is unweighted** and counts respondent-waves, so panelists appear up to three times.
- **Years are nominal**: the round's modal fieldwork year in the ESS, the election year in the CSES and EES.
- **Respondents without a type** (DK, unmatched, no vote item) are left out of the denominators, which assumes they distribute like the rest.
